results.fact: Trailhead parking pass at Killen Creek
results.evidence: The only conflicting copy is bivy[0].permit (a shared High Camp card). The Forest Service trail #113 page lists only the free self-issue wilderness permit and the Climbing Pass as required, and the Oregon Hikers field guide's fees section for this trailhead lists only the wilderness permit, which supports access.parking_pass. Note the evidence is not unanimous: WTA and an older wildflower guide still say a Northwest Forest Pass is required, so the camping clean-up should confirm with the Mt. Adams Ranger District before rewording the bivy card.

dist_km renders as the one-way APPROACH, not trailhead-to-summit. 8 km (about 5 mi) matches the walk to High Camp (3.1 mi Killen Creek Trail + 1.0 mi High Camp Trail) plus the short walk to the foot of the face below the Adams Glacier terminus; the summit climb is not part of the approach figure.

results.fact: When the route is in condition
results.evidence: Both documented descents of this face were on the weekend of mid-June; one report says good conditions come 'late in the spring' and the other notes the timing 'at least in mid June'. That is the Jun-Jul window the season chip and best_season give, so climate.spring is narrowed to late spring rather than all of spring.

patches.fact: When the route is in condition
patches.replace: Late spring, from about mid-June, is the firmest, most in-condition period.

results.correct_value: Above 7,000 ft (timberline), not only above high camp
results.evidence: The Forest Service summit page requires climbers to pack out human waste because decomposition above 7,000 ft is too slow; a second guide says solid waste must be packed out above timberline. Both put the line well below the Lunch Counter high camp, agreeing with access.rules and the bivy card.

results.evidence: One trip report gives the Adams Glacier with a North Ridge descent as c.16 miles round trip; two sources give about 17 mi round trip for the North Ridge (which shares this route's approach and descent). That suggests dist_km (17.5 mi, shown as one-way) is a round-trip figure and the itinerary's 13 mi total and the 11.5 mi summit pin are both off, but no second independent source states this route's own distance, and the 7-mile glacier-base pin is unsourced. A second route-specific distance (e.g. a club route page) would settle it.

The dispute is only with the shared High Camp bivy card. Outside sources partly support the card: the meadow stream at Adams Glacier Meadows runs until late summer and parties fill up at the glacial lake above camp. The camping clean-up should soften 'reliable through summer' rather than this route's approach text being changed.

results.fact: Number of days / camp after the climb

results.evidence: Three independent trip reports all climbed the Adams Glacier, descended the North Ridge and walked out to the trailhead the same day (one back in camp before 6 pm and at the trailhead about 8 pm, another at the car by 4:30 pm, a third at the car before sunset). The itinerary's two-day plan is right; the descent text's 'camp both before and after' is the outlier.

results.correct_value: About 17 mi round trip from Killen Creek (about 8.5 mi each way); summit day from High Camp about 8.8 mi
results.evidence: Two independent sources give the North Ridge from the Killen Creek trailhead as about 17 miles round trip. With the sourced 4.1 mi each way to High Camp (3.1 mi Killen Creek Trail + 1.0 mi High Camp Trail), the camp-summit-camp day is about 8.8 mi, not 4, and the summit is about 8.5 mi from the trailhead, not 11.5. dist_km (3.5 mi) is left: it renders as the one-way approach and matches the 3.5 mi walk to the PCT.

results.correct_value: The approach from High Camp to the ridge is snowfield and moraine, not glacier; glacier lies on the ridge's flanks and on the summit ice cap
results.evidence: From High Camp parties go up late-season snowfields and moraine to the cleaver and gain the ridge almost immediately after the lake above camp; the route is described as non-technical, with the only glacier travel being a corridor of unbroken glacier between the top of the ridge and the summit. The rack, protection and approach text are reworded to put the glacier gear on the ice cap and flanks rather than the approach.

results.fact: Distance to the base of the ridge

results.evidence: Parties leaving the lake about a mile above High Camp gain the ridge 'almost immediately', and another report goes straight from the lake up snowfields and moraine onto the cleaver. results.evidence: Dispute is only with the shared High Camp bivy card. Sources show a meadow stream at High Camp that may stop running late in summer, and a glacial lake above camp where parties fill up, so 'last reliable water' at East Fork Adams Creek is defensible while the card's 'reliable through summer' is overstated; left to the camping clean-up.

A guide service says the steepest sections of the North Ridge are around 40 degrees, and a route listing gives a maximum slope of about 40 degrees. The itinerary's 'around 40°' is right and max_angle 50 is the outlier.

No outside source found giving a recommended departure time for this route (one traverse party started at 7 a.m. from the car, which does not bear on a camp start). A published route description stating a start window would settle 2-3 AM vs 3-4 AM.

No source gives a distance for the Lyman Glacier route itself. The shared approach is 4.1 mi each way to High Camp, and the North Ridge descent route is about 17 mi round trip, which suggests the 14.2-mi itinerary total is short and dist_km (23.2 mi) is not a one-way figure, but neither can be set without a route-specific distance.

Dispute is only with the shared High Camp bivy card; the approach text's East Fork Adams Creek as last easy water is consistent with sources, while the card's 'reliable through summer' is overstated (the meadow stream may stop running late in summer). Left to the camping clean-up.

One source says the route turns up the steep headwall at about 11,300 ft; the main route description gives Sunrise Camp (8,300 ft) and the bergschrund (9,500 ft) but no headwall elevation. The 11,600-ft pin may mark the top of the headwall rather than its foot. A second source for where the headwall begins or ends would settle it.

The club route page for the Avalanche/White Salmon Glaciers from Cold Springs gives 6,700 ft of gain, and 5,000 ft appears only as the summit-day figure from a high camp. Only one source states the car-to-car figure, so gain_ft (and loss_ft) are not changed; a second route-specific gain figure would settle it.

The club route page calls this a glacier route on the SW slopes, and the Avalanche Glacier is described as lying on the west to southwest slopes of Mount Adams. The overview, beta and approach agree; aspect S and the face label 'South side' are corrected.
Trip reports and a trail guide give the Killen Creek trailhead at c.4,600 ft (the guide lists a low point of 4,600 ft), matching the trailhead pin and the camp card; 4,140 ft is the outlier.

results.evidence: The club route page gives 7,800 ft of gain for the Lava Glacier Headwall, which supports gain_ft; no source states a car-to-car descent figure, so loss_ft (5,000) and the itinerary's 6,700/6,700 are not changed. A route-specific loss or itinerary figure would settle it.

No source gives this route's distance. The shared North Ridge descent route is about 17 mi round trip from Killen Creek, which suggests the 12.5-mi itinerary is short and dist_km (16.5 mi) is a round-trip rather than a one-way figure, but neither can be set without a route-specific source.

The row's own corrections note says the rack was sized by analogy with neighbouring routes, and the club page gives no screw count. Sources describe the face as about 45-degree neve climbed continuously, which fits the protection text's 'occasional screw', but no source states a number, so neither copy is changed.
